record.paper_title: Properly Coloured Cycles and Paths: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the transformation method that converts an edge-coloured multigraph into an ordinary graph so that properly coloured cycle and properly coloured (s,t)-path problems can be solved via perfect matchings, determine an optimal transformation that minimizes the order and size of the transformed graph while preserving the needed correspondence with properly coloured subgraphs.

evidence.quote: We raise a problem of finding the optimal transformation and consider a possible solution to the problem.
We raise a problem of determining the minimum order and size of the transformed graph, and describe the family of graphs that may be the solution to the problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be an edge-coloured multigraph, where each edge has been assigned one colour from a finite set. A walk in G is properly coloured (PC) if any two consecutive edges along it have distinct colours; a PC cycle and a PC (s,t)-path are defined accordingly. It is known that the existence of a PC cycle in G, and the existence of a PC (s,t)-path between two prescribed vertices s and t, as well as finding shortest such subgraphs, can be reduced to perfect-matching computations in an auxiliary (uncoloured) graph H obtained from G by a suitable transformation T: G ↦ H, which preserves the bijective correspondence between PC cycles/paths of G and certain perfect matchings of H.

Among all such transformations T with this correspondence property, find one that simultaneously minimizes the order |V(H)| and the size |E(H)| of the transformed graph H, expressed as functions of the parameters of G (such as the number of vertices, the number of edges, and the number of colours). Equivalently, determine the minimum possible order and size of an auxiliary graph H that encodes, via its perfect matchings, the properly coloured cycles (respectively properly coloured (s,t)-paths) of an arbitrary edge-coloured multigraph G, and describe the family of graphs achieving this optimum.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding an optimal transformation from an edge-coloured multigraph to an ordinary graph (for reducing properly coloured cycle/path problems to perfect matching) is posed as an open question. No subsequent work resolving the minimum order and size of such a transformed graph was located in the search; related surveys on alternating/properly coloured paths and cycles continue to list transformation-based reductions without identifying a proven optimum.

status_evidence.title: Properly Coloured Cycles and Paths: Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Considers a family of transformations of an edge-coloured multigraph G into an ordinary graph that allow checking the existence of PC cycles and PC (s,t)-paths and finding shortest ones; raises the problem of finding the optimal transformation.
status_evidence.claim: The optimal-transformation problem is explicitly posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Alternating cycles and paths in edge-coloured multigraphs: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of reductions and results on alternating/properly coloured cycles and paths in edge-coloured multigraphs.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the optimal transformation question is reported in related surveys.
